newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Malan to decide on CPMF tax on stocks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Malan to decide on CPMF tax on stocks - paper.

text.p: Brazilian Finance Minister Pedro Malan will give the final word on whether foreign investors in local stocks will be exempt from the so-called CPMF tax, Gazeta Mercantil newspaper said.

The newspaper said the government is studying two alternatives regarding foreign investment in Brazil's stock market under Annex Four rules -- to allow foreigners to be exempt from the CPMF tax or charge the 0.2 percent tax only when the money comes in and is sent abroad after the shares are sold.
Gazeta also said that the government has already agreed that domestic investors in the bolsa will be subject to the new financial tax.

Government officials have expressed different opinions about the CPMF tax on stock transactions. Central Bank and Finance Ministry officials back the idea of protecting the bolsa, but the Internal Revenue Service and the Health Ministry have showed no interest in accepting exemptions.
The CPMF tax, created to finance Brazil's health services, will take effect on January 25.
A government decision on the issue is expected to come out in coming days.
